package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of the legitimate 'ionicons' package and contains obfuscated code that exfiltrates end-user form data to attacker-controlled domains. Its sole purpose is to deceive developers and steal sensitive user information from applications that include it.

execution_context.file_location: main package JavaScript file (e.g., index.js or distributed bundle)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attaches event listeners to all form elements in the DOM, intercepts form submissions, collects the form data, and sends it via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain (ionicio.com), resulting in exfiltration of sensitive user input.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating user form data to an external, attacker-controlled domain is a clear violation of user privacy and application security.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate icon package should only provide static assets or rendering logic for icons, not interact with the DOM or perform network requests on form submissions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or form-handling libraries may collect form data, but only with user consent and to trusted domains, not to lookalike or unrelated domains.
key_indicators: Network requests to a domain similar to the legitimate package's website (ionicio.com vs ionic.io)
No legitimate reason for an icon package to access or exfiltrate form data

attack_chain.action: Developer installs the malicious package (icon-package) instead of the legitimate one due to typosquatting.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in the application bundle.

attack_chain.action: When the application runs in a user's browser, the malicious code executes and attaches event listeners to all form elements.
On form submission, the code collects all form data and sends it to the attacker's domain (ionicio.com).
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive user data to the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in UI packages that attaches event listeners to all forms
Network requests to domains similar to legitimate package domains but with subtle typos
Obfuscated code that interacts with the DOM and performs data exfiltration
file_indicators: index.js or main bundle containing obfuscated code referencing 'form', 'addEventListener', and 'fetch' or 'XMLHttpRequest'
References to external domains not associated with the legitimate package
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to ionicio.com or other attacker-controlled domains (e.g., graph-googleapis.com, curls.safhosting.xyz, arpanrizki.my.id, dnster.my.id, okep.renznesia.xyz, ryucha.my.id, panelllgege.001www.com, nge.scrp.my.id, apiii-xyz.yogax.my.id, panel.archodex.xyz, panel.curlz.online)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript packages, especially those with names similar to popular libraries, that contain obfuscated code accessing the DOM and sending form data to external domains. Flag any network requests from UI or icon packages to domains not associated with the legitimate vendor, especially those with typosquatted names. Use static and dynamic analysis to detect code that attaches event listeners to forms and exfiltrates data.
